meta.what: The RT VENDOR + COST ledger. One row per vendor group the fleet can reach — its Telegram chat id, its Airtable Config record, its nominal reach, its full roster of X handles, and its cost model. This is the file that lets Project Infinity reason about RT logistics without asking the bot.
meta.why: Until now project-infinity held ZERO local vendor data. Every vendor fact came from a live Airtable read (6 fields: Name/Tier/Price/Network Size/Active/Chat ID) or from the one-shot map inside sync-vendor-chatids.mjs, which covered 17 of 22 vendors and had been stale since 2026-07-14 — VRT-EM (1.43M reach), VRT-Hey Brother and VRT-UYL were all onboarded in August 2026 and are invisible to Fuel the Fire to this day. Meanwhile genius-rt-bot carries 21 live vendors, 113 per-handle follower counts, and a three-branch cost model. This file closes that gap.
meta.sourceOfTruth: genius-rt-bot `DEFAULT_PRESETS` in telegram_bot.py. That block already declares itself authoritative (`_seed_default_presets`: 'Code is source of truth') and carries a per-vendor `rev` counter that force-syncs cost + handles into bot state when bumped. This file is DERIVED from it and inherits the same `rev`, so a vendor whose rev here is behind the bot's is provably stale.

ownership.genius-rt-bot: identity (chatId, title), roster (handles + follower counts), nominal reach, and the cost model. Changes originate here.
ownership.project-infinity: measurement — velocity lift (vendor-audit.mjs), commission per fuel dollar (facts.jsonl), realisation rate, and the measured reachable window. Never writes back to the bot's roster.
ownership.airtable Config table: runtime routing for Fuel the Fire only. DERIVED — never hand-edit a Chat ID or Price there; fix it at the bot and re-sync. (The 2026-07-14 migration had to correct Lifepad by hand in both directions precisely because this rule did not exist.)

costModels.per_post: Variable — we pay `cost.perPost` every time this vendor delivers. Most vendors.
costModels.retainer: Flat `cost.monthlyRetainer` for unlimited use; marginal cost of one more send is $0. VOPE ($650/mo) and Lewin ($350/mo). A per-fire efficiency figure computed on marginal cost alone will always rate these two as free — prorate the retainer into the window before comparing them to a per_post vendor.
costModels.free: Our own accounts (GTX, the All-VGNs bundle). $0 either way.

meta.reachBasis: `nominalReach` is the vendor's COMBINED FOLLOWER COUNT, not impressions, and not a measurement. docs/unit-economics.md measured T1 (Pammy + IP, 766k nominal) delivering ~145k head views — a realisation of about 19%, which is normal for the unit and not underdelivery. Divide by nominal reach to compare vendors; never to forecast views. `meta.realisation` is the fleet constant to multiply by.
meta.handleCaveat: Handles are the verification key, not decoration. genius-rt-bot resolves each to X's permanent numeric rest_id so an RT check survives a rename. Two onboarding near-misses are recorded in the bot: @takeactionD (a separate @takeaction exists and is NOT theirs) and @Unlockyourlife_ (their pitch said @Unlockyourlife, which does not exist). Matching the wrong handle silently fails every verification for that group.
meta.provenance: Generated from genius-rt-bot telegram_bot.py DEFAULT_PRESETS. `airtableConfigId` is lifted from sync-vendor-chatids.mjs — the only place that join has ever existed. `fuelLogName` maps a vendor to the name its fires carry in the Fuel Log `Tier Breakdown`, so vendor-audit.mjs can join spend to roster.
meta.howToUpdate: A vendor's roster or rate changes at the BOT: edit DEFAULT_PRESETS and bump that vendor's `rev`. Then regenerate this file and open the PR in the same change. Do not hand-edit rows here — a hand edit is invisible to the bot and re-creates exactly the drift this file exists to end.
meta.notInFuelLog: 11 of the 21 vendors below have never appeared by name in project-infinity's fire ledger. Seven of them are reachable only as an indivisible $8.60 block (see bundles.t0); the rest the bot serves for paying clients and the fleet has never bought.
openQuestions: What does a SINGLE-retweet vendor actually realise? The 19% constant is measured on a 15-30x repeat vendor and applied to everyone. Until a one-RT vendor is measured, cross-vendor $/1k comparisons are not evidence. genius-rt-bot's per-vendor confirm data plus Growth Log view snapshots could answer it.
Do any other vendors repeat-retweet? Only Pammy and IP are known to; the rest default to 1 and nobody has asked.
meta.costCorrection: 2026-09-03: an earlier draft of this file summed all seven members' bot per-post rates to $12.45 and called that the cost of going direct. That was wrong — it charged for ConquerMM, which the T0 arrangement does not, and used the bot's own delivery rates rather than the T0 ones. Direct and brokered cost the same. Use bundles.t0.memberCost for T0 fan-out costing, and a vendor's own cost.perPost only for a send the BOT makes. RESOLVED 2026-09-03: ConquerMM IS incremental, so direct T0 is $11.10 flat — no range, no assumption.
meta.nameCollisions: ME vs Maven/EM are different vendors and BOTH names are now confirmed correct (operator 2026-09-03): ME was a typo for EM and has been renamed; Maven/EM is Maven & EM, where EM is @EssentialMastry, and keeps its name. vendor-audit.mjs joins Fuel Log lines on the vendor NAME, so a mislabel silently misattributes spend and lift rather than erroring. byFuelName() matches exactly and consults `aliases`; never substring-match a vendor name.

sendingWindow.what: The real window vendors act in, not an inherited client policy — this file previously carried it as an open question and it is now answered.
sendingWindow.consequence: That makes the overlap finding REAL rather than suggestive. Every THREAD publish window in slots.mjs falls entirely outside it: morning 06:00-07:30 SGN, afternoon 13:00-15:30, harvest 04:00-07:00 and viral 13:00-15:00 are all 0% overlap; only singles (13:00-22:00 SGN) overlaps, at 44%. All 271 T0 pings fired into a window the vendors were not in.
sendingWindow.rootCause: The fleet publishes when ITS audience is awake (Saigon afternoon) and vendors retweet when THEY are awake (US morning). Those are eleven hours apart, so no publish schedule satisfies both. The fix is to DECOUPLE the RT ping from publish time — publish at the audience-optimal hour, queue the ping for the next vendor window. That costs nothing and needs no vendor to change anything.
sendingWindow.status: RECORDED, NOT WIRED (operator, 2026-09-03: 'don't implement this yet').
sendingWindow.whyNotWired: The window being confirmed is knowledge worth having; acting on it is a change to how posts get delivered, and the delivery system works today. So the fact is recorded here and NOTHING reads it to decide a send: no vendor carries a `window`, inSendingWindow() falls back to reporting basis 'unmeasured', and holding stays inert exactly as it was before. To wire it later: stamp {tz:'America/New_York', startMin:420, endMin:720} onto the vendors it should apply to, and pass respectWindows:true / --hold-offhours at the call site. Both are opt-in and default OFF, so wiring is two deliberate steps, not a flag flip.

meta.realisationWarning: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING VENDORS ON $/1k. The 0.19 constant was measured on T1 — Pammy + IP, 766k nominal delivering ~145k head views (docs/unit-economics.md). Those two retweet each post 15-30 TIMES, so the 145k already contains that repetition: it is what 15-30 retweets produced. Applying the same constant to a vendor that retweets ONCE assumes a single retweet realises as well as fifteen, which is almost certainly false and generous to every vendor except Pammy and IP. So the per-1k column ranks vendors on an assumption calibrated from the one vendor pair it disadvantages. T1 is the ONLY tier with a measured delivery number ($24.50 -> ~145k head views = $0.169 per 1k, measured). Every other figure is a model. Do not rank vendors on it.
